In the following snippet I was trying to provide an alternate prove to List.reverseRec than the one found in Mathlib, and I noticed that rcases was unable to destruct an existential where cases could.

I understand that the error message that rcases gives me, since motive _ is not necessarily Prop. However, it seems like using cases here simply forces the motive to be in Prop, and I'm not too sure why there's this differnece in behaviour.

If I understand correctly, the main difference between rcases and cases is that rcases allows chaining recursively the use of primitive recursors, whereas cases can also use recursors introduced by the induction_eliminator and cases_eliminator attribute, but I don't see immediately how this could explain this discrepancy. Is there a way to query for the cases_eliminators registered to a type?

Well, rcases uses docs#Lean.MVarId.cases from Lean.Meta.Tactic.Cases and cases has it's own implementation in Lean.Elab.Tactic.Induction. These two share almost no code, so naturally they behave slightly differently.

Indeed, I knew about the different behaviours of these tactics before, I just found it weird the discrepancy in this case. I guess the title of the question should be more something along the lines of "Why does using cases here forces Sort _ to be interpreted as Prop, but rcases just gives a failure?".

But maybe you're right that the answer is just an uninteresting "well, they work differently, so it just so happens to work like this for this case"
But what I was curious about originally was what kind of mechanism made cases succeed here

Okay, it seems like MVarId.induction has a syntactic check for the universe (checking "is the universe exactly zero" here) and the induction and cases tactics just rely on unifying the motive types here which just ends up assigning the universe metavariable.
Thanks a lot for your time in finding it! This is exactly the type of thing I was wondering about
